newsitem.title: UK: North Sea Brent trades higher, CFDs active.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent trades higher, CFDs active.

text.p: North Sea Brent paper markets saw a firmer start on Wednesday despite a drop in outright levels, traders said.

Good buying on the CFD market for July 14-18 brought levels up in an otherwise bearish market. Traders attributed the gains to the tightness on North Sea crudes and, although they felt it would be short-lived, end-user buying was expected to support physical differentials for July loading barrels, they said.
Next week's (July 14-18) dates started the day bid at Sept -25 cents but traded at -20 and again at -17 cents as traders saw the week undervalued in the current tight physical market.

The July 14-18/21-25 roll widened over the morning from around three cents to trade at six cents. July 21-25 was valued at Sept -23/-21 cents. The two week July 14-18/July 28-01 roll traded at +7 cents.
Intermonth spreads talked around +22/25 for July/Aug and -10/-8 cents for Aug/Sept. The latter spread traded earlier at -10 cents.

A July 21-23 Brent cargo traded on Wednesday at August Brent +10 cents, up five cents from a deal on Tuesday. The buyer of Wednesday's cargo was heard to now have four cargoes in this time range destined for the U.S.
It was not clear, however, if the oil company was going to take a VLCC or the larger ULCC transatlantic.
Some traders were looking at the Mediterranean market as a possible source of Brent buying interest over the next week.
"Urals is very strong and if the refiners can't get Urals they will need to look at alternatives. Some grades are already going there," one major said.
At least two cargoes of Oseberg were heard destined for Mediterranean refineries.
